method: Official pages opened and substantive passages read with page_fetch on 2026-11-12 and again on 2026-11-13 for every claim published in this edition (session bd0afb0a, audit file session-bd0afb0a/VERIFICATION.md). Three published statements were corrected after that re-read: the 2026 SALT amount's supporting link, a ballot percentage, and the label applied to the 1% surtax. This remains a bounded audit of the public guide, not of Git history, forks or prior editions. Official-context links do not verify household data, private bills or synthetic assumptions.

estate.title: IRS · Estate tax
estate.finding: 2026 filing threshold $15,000,000; gross estate can include cash, securities, real estate, insurance and trusts; adjusted taxable gifts affect filing; deductions and credits affect liability. Re-read 2026-11-16: filing threshold table shows 2026 year of death $15,000,000.

irs27.title: IRS · 2027 inflation adjustments
irs27.finding: IR-2026-133 dated November 5, 2026 explicitly states 2027 basic estate exclusion $15,480,000, 2026 $15,000,000. This is published, not a forecast.

faq.title: IRS · Estate tax FAQ
faq.finding: Form 706 generally due nine months after death; six-month filing extension; portability requires filing; nonresident noncitizens require separate rules.

boe.title: California BOE · Proposition 19
boe.finding: Transferor/transferee principal residence, eligible relationship, adjusted value limit; homeowners exemption within one year; exclusion claim within three years or before third-party transfer. Official page lists 2026/026 guidance. Re-read 2026-11-16: comparison table confirms file homeowners exemption within 1 year of transfer and claim for exclusion within 3 years or before transfer to a third party.

allow.title: BOE · 2025 allowance notice
allow.finding: Allowance is $1,044,586 for transfers February 16, 2025 through February 15, 2027. Indexed every other year using California FHFA HPI, not general CPI.

rtc.title: California · RTC §51
rtc.finding: Factored base inflation increase capped at 2%; taxable value generally lesser of factored base and current full cash value. Temporary market reductions need not recover at only 2%.

trust.title: California · Probate Code §16061.7
trust.finding: Trustee notification triggered by specified events; generally 60 days, with awareness/vacancy exceptions. Does not itself establish all appraisal/insurance steps.

sco.title: California Controller · Estate tax
sco.finding: No California estate tax return for deaths on/after January 1, 2005; inheritance tax administered for pre-June 8, 1982 deaths.

basis.title: IRS · Inherited property basis
basis.finding: Generally date-of-death FMV basis, or elected alternate valuation where applicable; gain on sale above basis may be taxable.

trustbasis.title: IRS · Revenue Ruling 2023-2
trustbasis.finding: Bulletin synopsis expressly says §1014 adjustment generally does not apply to irrevocable grantor trust assets not included in deceased grantor gross estate.

sell.title: IRS · Topic 701
sell.finding: Home-sale exclusion up to $250,000/$500,000 if qualified; generally ownership/use two of five years; inheritance alone does not satisfy use.

rent.title: IRS · Topic 414
rent.finding: Rent taxable, deductible expenses subject to rules, depreciation, personal-use allocation, passive limitations and possible NIIT; capital improvements differ from repairs. Re-read 2026-11-16: Topic 414 taxes cash or fair market value of property or services actually received for the use of real estate; depreciation is an allowance under the same topic.

ftb.title: California FTB · Capital gains
ftb.finding: California has no preferential lower capital-gains rate; gains taxed as ordinary income. Re-read 2026-11-16 (page last updated 01/28/2026): California does not have a lower rate for capital gains; all capital gains are taxed as ordinary income.

insurance.title: California DOI · Residential insurance
insurance.finding: Compare coverage and premiums; official comparison tools linked. FAIR Plan limited perils and possible separate DIC coverage. No property-specific premium verified.

cpuc.title: California PUC · Customer generation
cpuc.finding: NEM bill credits differ from net billing; NBT applies to new interconnection applicants since April 15, 2023. No household cash profit established.

tenantlaw.title: California Legislature · Civil Code §1947.12
tenantlaw.finding: California's statewide residential rent cap has statutory exceptions, including housing subject to lower local limits. Applicability depends on facts; this source does not establish any household property coverage.

bill.title: California Legislature · SB 974
bill.finding: Chapter 665 approved September 27, 2026; special-needs trusts as eligible transfer medium. Enacted, not pending; household applicability unknown; no blanket Prop 19 repeal.

sec.title: SEC · Asset allocation and diversification
sec.finding: Allocation depends on time horizon and risk tolerance; diversification and rebalancing; no guaranteed return.

fdic.title: FDIC · Deposit insurance
fdic.finding: $250,000 per depositor per insured bank per ownership category; deposits aggregated within category; stocks, mutual funds, bonds not covered.

inflation.title: Federal Reserve History · Great Inflation
inflation.finding: 1965–1982 inflation regime included recessions and energy shocks; inflation exceeded 14% in 1980. Narrative context, not local property/portfolio returns.

recession.title: Federal Reserve History · Great Recession
recession.finding: National home prices approximately -30% mid-2006 to mid-2009; S&P500 price index -57% October 2007 to March 2009. Different peak/trough windows, not annual total returns or local forecasts.

cpi.title: BLS · Historical CPI-U
cpi.finding: Historical monthly and annual CPI-U table; the annual-percent-change column is the source of the decade table on the black-swan page. Arithmetic only: not a 50-year forecast and not California's statutory indexing series.

pages.title: GitHub Docs · Pages and data collection
pages.finding: Pages publishes static repository files through a build; GitHub states visitor IP addresses are logged for security, even when visitors are not signed in.

history.title: GitHub Docs · Sensitive-data removal
history.finding: Rewriting history alone does not remove clones/forks, cached views or PR references. Removal requires coordination; other users’ clones cannot be erased by the repository owner. No history rewrite is performed here.

sched_a.title: IRS · Schedule A Instructions (SALT cap)
sched_a.finding: The 2025 Schedule A instructions state the overall state and local tax limit is $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately), reduced when modified AGI exceeds $500,000 but never below $10,000. This link does not state the later-year amount; that is flagged separately.

saltlaw.title: Congress.gov · Public Law 119-21 §70120 (individual SALT limit)
saltlaw.finding: Section 70120 amends IRC §164(b)(6)-(7): the individual SALT itemized-deduction cap is $40,000 for 2025 and $40,400 for 2026, with 101% annual increases for 2027-2029; after 2029 it is $10,000. For 2025-2029 the cap is reduced by 30% of modified AGI above $500,000 (2025), $505,000 (2026), then a 101%-indexed threshold, but not below $10,000; MFS amounts are half. Applies to tax years beginning after Dec. 31, 2024. Statutory schedule, not a forecast or property-specific rental-tax calculation.

boepub.title: BOE · Publication 800-1 (Prop 19)
boepub.finding: BOE-266 homeowners exemption must precede BOE-19-P; claims timely within 3 years (before transfer) or 6 months of supplemental notice; moving out cancels exclusion next Jan 1 lien date and enrolls indexed date-of-death FMV.

ftb540.title: CA FTB · 2025 Form 540 Booklet
ftb540.finding: 2025 Form 540 instructions, Line 62 'Behavioral Health Services Tax': if taxable income is more than $1,000,000, compute 1% of the amount above $1,000,000 (read 2026-11-16). The booklet does not state a prior name; no rename history is asserted here.

sos26.title: CA Secretary of State · 2026 Ballot Measures
sos26.finding: Unofficial returns read 2026-11-16: as of November 14, 2026, 5:16 p.m., 23,860 of 23,860 precincts, Prop 3 Yes 60.7%, Prop 40 No 52.2%, Prop 41 No 55.2%, Prop 42 Yes 51.3%, Prop 43 No 57.6%; certification is due by December 11, 2026. No Prop 19 repeal appeared on the November 2026 ballot.

revproc.title: IRS · Rev. Proc. 2026-35 (2027 adjustments)
revproc.finding: Section 3.44: basic exclusion amount for estate tax under §2010(c)(3) is $15,480,000 for 2027. Section 3.46: 2027 annual gift exclusion is $20,000. Federal figures only; not a per-heir allowance.

lta26002.title: California BOE · LTA 2026/002 (2026-27 CCPI)
lta26002.finding: 2026-27 assessment roll inflation factor is 1.02: CCPI +3.307% (August 2024 to August 2025, because October 2025 was not published after the federal shutdown), capped at 2% under Art. XIII A §2(b).

lta25009.title: California BOE · LTA 2025/009 (value-cap adjustment)
lta25009.finding: Intergenerational transfer value cap is the factored base-year value plus $1,044,586 for transfers from Feb 16, 2025 to Feb 15, 2027. The amount is next adjusted in February 2027, using the FHFA California House Price Index.

lta26026.title: California BOE · Prop 19 FAQ (LTA 2026/026, Aug 3, 2026)
lta26026.finding: Defines a transfer as including transfers at death, whether within or outside a trust. A family home is a dwelling eligible for the homeowners' exemption from the transferor's ownership and occupation, with a reasonable site area. A continual-use requirement applies. Board guidance summary, not statute.

cdires.title: CA DOI · Residential Insurance Guide (Form 401)
cdires.finding: Standard homeowners policies exclude earthquake, flood, earth movement, mold, wear/tear and losses to a dwelling vacant 60+ days.

cpucfixed.title: CPUC · Resolution E-5354 (Base Services Charge)
cpucfixed.finding: Resolution E-5354 approves with modifications PG&E’s income-graduated fixed-charge implementation plan. It does not state a property-specific bill or establish a universal fixed charge for every utility or rate plan.

water.title: California Water Boards · Find your water system
water.finding: The State Water Board page links an official map to identify a public drinking-water system service area from a residential address. It does not publish the property’s water or wastewater rates; those must be checked with the actual provider.

t117043.title: California · RTC §17043 (1% additional tax)
t117043.finding: For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2005, an additional tax of 1 percent is imposed on the portion of a taxpayer's taxable income above $1,000,000. The threshold is not adjusted for filing status by this section.

treas26.title: U.S. Treasury · Daily par yield curve, November 2026
treas26.finding: Read 2026-11-16. Par yields for 2026-11-13: 3-month 4.32%; 2-year 4.88%; 10-year 5.15%. Yields move daily; re-read the page at each decision date.

irc6075.title: IRS · Instructions for Form 706 (Rev. July 2026), When To File
irc6075.finding: 'You must file Form 706 to report estate and/or GST tax within 9 months after the date of the decedent’s death.' Automatic 6-month extension on Form 4768, which can also request an extension of time to pay. Filing threshold for 2026 deaths: $15,000,000 (Which Estates Must File). Read 2026-11-16. Statute: IRC §6075(a).

irc1031.title: U.S. Code · 26 U.S.C. §1031 (GPO, 2024 edition)
irc1031.finding: Section 1031(a)(1): real property held for productive use in a trade or business or for investment, exchanged solely for like-kind property held for the same purposes. (a)(3): identification within 45 days and completion within 180 days (or the return due date, if earlier). Read 2026-11-16. Receipt requirement also restated in IRS Publication 544 (2025), Like-Kind Exchanges, read 2026-11-16 (180th day or return due date, if earlier).

irc1250.title: Cornell LII · 26 U.S.C. §1250 (non-government mirror of the statute)
irc1250.finding: Section 1250(a)(1)(A): additional depreciation (excess over straight-line) on disposition is treated as ordinary income, to the extent of the gain. Read 2026-11-16 from a non-government mirror; the official GPO copy was not retrieved (flagged 9B-F1). Unrecaptured-section-1250 federal rates in IRC §1(h) not read.

fred_tb3ms.title: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED · 3-month Treasury bill, annual average
fred_tb3ms.finding: Read 2026-11-16. Series starts 1934-01, so no official bill value exists for 1928-1933. Annual averages used here run 1934-2025; 2026 has no complete year. Annual average for 2025 was 4.07 percent.

fred_gs2.title: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED · 2-year Treasury constant maturity, annual average
fred_gs2.finding: Read 2026-11-16. Series starts 1976-06; annual averages used here run 1977-2025. A par yield is not a total return; it is used only as a holding-price proxy for the parked 2-year leg.

irs403.title: IRS Topic 403 · Interest received
irs403.finding: Read 2026-11-16. Interest income from Treasury bills, notes and bonds is subject to federal income tax but is exempt from all state and local income taxes.

hist_returns.title: S&P 500 annual total return, 1928-2025 · academic series (not a government source)
hist_returns.finding: Page read 2026-11-16 and labelled January 2026. The 1928-2025 column used here was checked against the repository copy at 31 sample years with no mismatch. This is a non-government academic series and is flagged as such on the page that uses it.

saltcorr.title: IRS · Correction to the state and local tax deduction amount in the 2026 Form 1040-ES
saltcorr.finding: For 2026 the limit is $40,400 ($20,200 if married filing separately); the overall limit is reduced if modified AGI is more than $505,000 ($252,500 if married filing separately) but not below $10,000 ($5,000 if married filing separately). Read 2026-11-16. This page states only 2026; the 2027-2029 amounts are arithmetic on the statute (101% of the prior year) in the congress.gov entry.
